questions.question: What does "RQ" stand for?
questions.explanation: On shipping papers, "RQ" can be used instead of "X" in the hazardous materials column when a reportable quantity of the material needs to be marked.

questions.question: If cargo with hazardous materials is leaking, the driver should:

options.text: Drive to find a phone to alert emergency personnel
Drive to a designated hazardous materials clean up facility
Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and contact emergency personnel
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials are leaking, stop driving immediately. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and send someone to get help. Continuing to drive spreads contamination over a larger area.

questions.question: ____ identical placards must be placed on a vehicle transporting hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: When hazardous materials placards are required, place them on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: If you apply for a HazMat endorsement, which agency must check your background?
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check with the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading must:

options.text: Does not have to be able to move the vehicle.
Does not need to know about the materials being loaded.
Stay within 25 feet of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: A supervisor must stay within 25 feet of the tank, watch it closely, have a clear view, know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations are meant to protect:
questions.explanation: Transporting hazardous materials is risky. The regulations protect you, people around you, and the environment.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. The only exception is if you need to run the engine to operate a pump.

questions.question: To drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, a driver must have:

options.text: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
A CDL with a passenger endorsement.
A CDL with an air brake endorsement.

questions.correctAnswerText: A CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement.
questions.explanation: You need a commercial driver license with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle used to transport hazardous materials, even if it is not carrying them at the time.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs, called placards, on all four sides.

questions.question: How must a shipper notify a driver of cargo risks?

options.text: By writing a note on a blank piece of paper
By putting hazard warning labels on packages
By placing orange dots on packages

questions.correctAnswerText: By putting hazard warning labels on packages
questions.explanation: Shippers must notify drivers of hazards using shipping papers, hazard labels on packages, emergency response information, and placards.

questions.question: A package with liquid containers must show:

options.text: Arrows pointing the correct upright direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Packages with liquid containers must show arrows pointing the correct upright direction. This tells handlers which way to position the package.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, you can leave your vehicle unattended at:
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous materials, you can only leave your vehicle unattended at a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: Your shipment likely contains hazardous materials if:

options.text: The shipper works in a business like fireworks sales or pest control.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The shipper is located in a bad part of town.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper works in a business like fireworks sales or pest control.
questions.explanation: A good sign that your shipment contains hazardous materials is that the shipper works in a business that typically handles dangerous items. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, and pest control firms.

questions.question: Shipping papers for hazardous materials should be placed:

options.text: At the bottom of the stack.

questions.explanation: Drivers and carriers need to find hazardous materials papers quickly. Hazardous materials papers must be on top of all other papers.

questions.question: For small packages that cannot fit a HazMat label, use:
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a proper label, attach the label to a tag. Secure the tag firmly to the package.

questions.question: How many hazardous materials classes exist?
questions.explanation: There are nine hazardous materials classes. Each class describes the risks of that type of material.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous products are also flammable. Take proper safety steps if you think your cargo may be flammable.

questions.question: When watching a tank being loaded or unloaded, you should do everything below except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: A supervisor watching a hazardous materials tank must stay alert, remain within 25 feet, have a clear view, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank. A chemical suit is not required.

questions.question: The person loading a hazardous materials tank must do everything below except:

options.text: Stay within 10 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.
Be able to move the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 10 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: The supervisor must stay alert, have a clear view, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank. Staying within 10 feet is not required.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tire with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of each trip and after each stop. A tire pressure gauge is the only correct way to check tire pressure.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a shipping paper?
questions.explanation: Shipping papers describe hazardous materials being transported. Shipping orders, bills of lading, and manifests are all shipping papers.

questions.question: To complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest, you must:

options.text: Sign only if you cross into another state.
Sign only if the weather was hazardous.

questions.explanation: You must sign a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest by hand. The manifest must also show the name and EPA registration number of the shipper, carrier, and destination.

questions.question: When seated behind the steering wheel, shipping papers should be:

options.text: Taped to the passenger's side window.

questions.explanation: Keep shipping papers where you can easily reach them while wearing your seat belt. Keep them in a pouch in the driver's side door or another easy-to-reach place. They must be visible to anyone entering the cab.

questions.question: Shipping papers:

options.text: Are not needed for most shipments.
Should be stored in a special compartment in the cab.
Can be kept as a digital file.

questions.explanation: All hazardous materials shipments require shipping papers. These papers inform drivers and dockworkers about the risks of the cargo.

questions.question: Hazardous materials laws are controlled by:
questions.explanation: Because hazardous materials are dangerous, federal, state, and local governments can all make rules about how they are transported.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle:

options.text: Can only be moved in an emergency.
Can be driven if it does not contain radioactive materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only be moved in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials vehicles must have proper placards to be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle may only be driven in an emergency to protect life or property.

questions.question: Who is responsible for identifying the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product's identification number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, it is important to know that:

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
The packages should be carried in the cab.
The packages should be loaded on their side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation passes through packages to nearby packages. Because of this, there are limits on how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: When loading a tank with flammable liquids:

options.text: A ground should be established before opening the filling hole.
A ground should be broken right before opening the filling hole.
The filling hole should be locked during loading.

questions.correctAnswerText: A ground should be established before opening the filling hole.
questions.explanation: Before loading or unloading a tank with flammable liquids, turn off the engine unless it is needed to run a pump. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until after closing the filling hole.

questions.question: When a driver is not in their vehicle, hazardous materials shipping papers should be:
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must always be easy to access. When the driver is not in the vehicle, leave hazardous materials shipping papers on the driver's seat.
